children: Townsquare Media rejected a buyout proposal from Hoffmann Family of Cos. that it said significantly undervalued the company.
"Our Board and management team have full confidence in Townsquare's strategy and the strength of our business," the company said.
Townsquare's operations include 342 radio stations, including NJ101.5, and websites such as Loudwire, XXL, Taste of Country and ScreenCrush.

On Nov. 16, multiple media outlets including St. Louis Magazine reported the approach from David Hoffmann, who led an investment in Lee Enterprises earlier this year and became chairman. The stock closed that day at $1.28.
Shares of Townsquare rose 7.7% in late trading after finishing the market session up 2.6% at $1.17.
Write to Josh Beckerman at josh.beckerman@wsj.com
This article was corrected at 7:10 p.m. ET. to reflect the proper name of David Hoffmann. The original article incorrectly spelled his last name as Hoffman.
Correction to Townsquare Media Rejects Buyout Proposal Article

David Hoffmann led an investment in Lee Enterprises earlier this year and became chairman. "Townsquare Media Rejects Hoffmann Family Buyout Proposal," at 6:46 p.m. ET, incorrectly said his name was David Hoffman.
